advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm intended handling of container criteria with zero reviewed children and, if withheld, record a reason distinct from unrecoverable-material.
evidence: fixture_admission.py:337: if not isinstance(children, list) or not children: return False
No test covers a container criterion with an empty reviewed-children list; the two new admission tests use non-empty rosters (child dicts) or legacy bare strings.
advisory.finding: `_children_are_replayable` returns False for a container criterion whose review legitimately named zero children (`not children` at fixture_admission.py:337), so such a case is withheld as `unrecoverable-material` rather than admitted. If a container criterion (G3/G4/decomp-shape) can validly be scored over an empty roster, this silently withholds a faithful case; if it cannot, an empty roster is arguably a corpus/reconstruction anomaly worth a distinct reason. Either way the empty-roster world is folded into 'unrecoverable-material' without distinction.
scenarios: A historical container review that recorded no reviewed child material reaches admission with children=[] and is withheld as unrecoverable-material.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a fixture_admission test where a container criterion's child dict has empty-string title/description (recoverable CREATE, no title) and assert the intended verdict (withheld vs admitted).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/evals/fixture_admission.py:344: `if not isinstance(child.get("title"), str) or not isinstance(child.get("description"), str):` — empty strings pass this check
src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/corpus.py:272: `"title": str(title or ""),` — a recoverable child CREATE with no title yields title='' yet children_reconstructed=True

ABSENCE: tests/unit/test_fixture_admission.py adds test_container_criterion_admits_with_rehydrated_child_material (non-empty title/description) and test_container_criterion_with_legacy_child_strings_is_unrecoverable (bare strings), but no case with a child dict carrying title='' / description=''
src/rebar/llm/evals/fixture_admission.py:339-345: the loop returns False if ANY child lacks a str title/description

ABSENCE: the new admission tests use uniform rosters — all-dict (test_container_criterion_admits_with_rehydrated_child_material) or all-bare-string (test_container_criterion_with_legacy_child_strings_is_unrecoverable); no children=[full_dict, 'bare-string'] mix
advisory.finding: _children_are_replayable treats a child with empty-string title/description as replayable (isinstance('', str) is True), so a container criterion whose child has a recoverable CREATE but empty/blank title (children_reconstructed=True) is dispatched to the finder over impoverished content — the exact impoverished-roster case the diff's rationale claims to guard against. No test exercises a child dict with title='' / description='' (or a recoverable child CREATE with no title field).
merged_from: A MIXED child roster (some children full title/description dicts, others bare-string ids or missing-CREATE) for a container criterion is untested. The added _children_are_replayable returns False on the first non-conforming child, so a partial roster is withheld — a behavior path with no regression coverage.
scenarios: A reviewed child ticket whose CREATE event omitted a title, or whose title/description were empty at review time

Container criteria include decomp-shape (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/container_stage.py:36 `CONTAINER_CRITERIA = ("G3", "G4", "decomp-shape")`), which may legitimately score a childless/empty decomposition.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider having admission consume the persisted `children_reconstructed` flag (or drop it) rather than re-deriving replayability, to keep a single source of truth.
evidence: _child_materials only omits title/description when create_found is False (corpus.py:264-267), which is exactly when reconstructed=False — so the two are aligned today, but the admission path never reads the persisted flag.
dropped.finding: The corpus persists an explicit `children_reconstructed` boolean (corpus.py:320) recording whether every child's material was recoverable, but the admission runner ignores that flag and independently re-derives replayability from the child-dict shape via `_children_are_replayable` (fixture_admission.py:336-346). Two separate oracles encode the same property; a future change to one (e.g. corpus stores partial title but not description) could silently desync the persisted flag from the admission gate.
scenarios: A later corpus change persists partial child material (title only) — the persisted `children_reconstructed` and the admission-side `_children_are_replayable` verdicts diverge.
